rules: Index polygons were historically captured on OS county-series sheets, national-grid sheets and parcel books.
HMLR completed conversion of 19 million paper index polygons to vector polygons in February 2004.
The 2004 vectorised polygons were mapped against OS Land-Line.
HMLR's Positional Accuracy Improvement programme ran from 2005 to 2008.
Many PAI changes were automated, while records outside criteria were referred for manual title-plan comparison.
The Quality Improvement Flowline processed almost 14 million index polygons around 2009.
Daily OS MasterMap change-only updates support new polygons and plans rather than routine review of existing registrations.
Large-scale OS mapping used by HMLR can be captured at 1:1,250 in urban areas.
Large-scale OS mapping used by HMLR can be captured at 1:2,500 in semi-urban and rural areas.
Large-scale OS mapping used by HMLR can be captured at 1:10,000 in mountain and moorland areas.
Artificial footprints may divide large multi-level developments into smaller indexing areas.
Exaggerated extents use a minimum one-metre width so narrow registered strips remain identifiable.
Former gridding practice can split one real-world feature at national-grid sheet joins into separate polygon IDs.
Publication validation removes zero-area polygons and polygons below 0.1 square metres.
Exact current Barnet and Enfield INSPIRE GML bytes and hashes remain unavailable.

The entity endpoint supports filtering by start-date year.
The entity endpoint supports filtering by start-date month.
The entity endpoint supports filtering by start-date day.
Start-date matching supports match, before, since or an empty value.
The entity endpoint supports filtering by end-date year.
The entity endpoint supports filtering by end-date month.
The entity endpoint supports filtering by end-date day.
End-date matching supports match, before, since or an empty value.
Entry-date filtering is available by year, month and day.
Entry-date matching supports match, before, since or an empty value.
Spatial relations include within, equals, disjoint, intersects, touches, contains, covers, coveredby, overlaps and crosses.

The official one-metre composite DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
Surface objects are removed from the DSM using bespoke algorithms and manual editing.
The 2022 composite combines the Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest best-resolution data is used.
Bilinear interpolation is used where source data is resampled before merging.
The 2022 composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022.
Downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in five-kilometre tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevations are in metres, referenced to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and transformed using OSTN15.
The dataset records an annual update frequency.

The contour GML model is feature-based with ContourLine, SpotHeight and LandWaterBoundary feature types.
ContourLine types include master, ordinary and auxiliary.
Current spot-height features use the generic subtype while other subtype values are reserved for future enrichment.
OS Terrain 50 feature identifiers follow os.t50.<tile name>.<sequential number>.
Geometry identifiers use the same feature identifier with a .geom suffix.
Updates use whole-tile refresh and no feature-based change-only update is planned.
OS Terrain 50 GML expresses British National Grid as urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::27700.
